lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Owned the weekly carrier scorecards for the regional managers and the monthly review meeting that discussed them.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: The résumé has no summary or target-role framing.
items.because: Readers have to infer that you are pursuing product management.

items.says: The product and operations experience does not form an immediately coherent career story.
items.because: The résumé does not explicitly connect that experience to a clear next step in product management.

items.says: Only one clearly titled product-management role is shown, and it was an internship.
items.because: No explicit post-MBA PM role appears on the résumé.

items.says: Product strategy, go-to-market, and product-lifecycle evidence is not listed.
items.because: Some PM openings may require those capabilities.

items.says: Some bullets describe activities without clearly distinguishing them from measured product outcomes.
items.because: The scope or outcome of the contribution can be hard to see.

items.says: Consider whether the education location is worth its space.
items.because: Locations do not help establish PM fit.

items.says: Consider whether the education location is worth its space.
items.because: Locations do not help establish PM fit.

items.says: The current Diesel Mechanic role makes the post-MBA career direction hard to read.
items.because: It is a surprising endpoint after an MBA and product internship.

items.says: Explain the PM relevance of the engine and gearbox rebuild work.
items.because: Without its operational constraints, coordination, or reliability outcomes, it may look like a sharp departure from product experience.

items.says: The maintenance and inspection-record bullet lacks a meaningful outcome.
items.because: It reads as routine maintenance and recordkeeping rather than distinctive PM-relevant evidence.

items.says: The carrier-scorecard bullet does not show what changed because of the work.
items.because: It establishes responsibility but gives no scale, decision informed, or improvement produced.

items.says: Clarify the measurement period for the pick-error reduction.
Add the business consequence of fewer pick errors, if known.
Define what the forecast-error measure represents.
Clarify whether the forecast-error reduction held over 12 quarters or was the final observed result.
The route-planning bullet combines too many activities.
items.because: Rollout, SOP changes, training, and negotiations obscure the measured impact.

items.says: Clarify how the annual driver hours saved were estimated.
Explain how time to first payment was calculated.
Clarify whether the onboarding result covers the whole pilot cohort or only a subset.
Keep the checkout-conversion unit of change precise.
items.because: Going from 61% to 66% is a five-percentage-point increase, not a 5% increase.

items.says: Clarify what shipping the flow to all merchants covers.
Say whether the measured conversion lift was sustained after rollout.
Clarify how Reach was scored in the RICE method.
items.because: Tickets a feature would close may describe expected support-ticket reduction rather than conventional Reach.

items.says: The activity sequence obscures what roadmap decision you influenced.
Distinguish your recommendation from the final decision-maker’s authority.
items.because: Your role in setting the priority is unclear.

items.says: The checkout A/B-test bullet repeats the conversion result claimed in the earlier checkout bullet.
items.because: It does not clearly add a distinct contribution.

items.says: Be exact about what was randomized and what the reported outcome measures.
items.because: Session-level assignment and customer conversion are related but not the same unit.

items.says: Clarify whether the additional rollout was funded or actually deployed.
items.because: Approval for a plan should not be confused with deployment.

items.says: Define what the 3,100 students represent.
items.because: They could be students reached, registered, or eligible to use the app.

items.says: Clarify whether the 9 tonnes reflects measured redistribution.
Support the description of the food as otherwise wasted.
The stated 150% weekly-active-user increase is incorrect.
items.because: An increase from 400 to 1,150 is 187.5%.

items.says: Clarify the period over which weekly active users increased.
Clarify whether both user figures use the same WAU definition.
The fill-rate change is called a 20% increase rather than a 20-percentage-point increase.
items.because: The rate went from 75% to 95%.

items.says: Clarify the fill-rate measurement period.
Clarify whether the fill-rate change was observed consistently across both halls.
Distinguish the modeled annual saving from realized savings.
items.because: Pilot funding is not evidence that the full projected saving was achieved.

items.says: Clarify your role in the patient-intake work.
items.because: The passive construction hides what you did.

items.says: Clarify the actual patient-intake change adopted.
Give the effect of the intake change, if measured.
items.because: The bullet does not show its effect on intake time, completion, or staff workload.

items.says: The pilot-approval outcome repeats the approval in the first practicum bullet.
items.because: It spends space on the same outcome twice rather than a separate contribution.

items.says: The product skills list does not show depth or scope.
items.because: It names methods rather than the strongest capabilities evidenced in the experience.

items.says: The tools list is short and does not say what each tool was used for.
items.because: It gives limited coverage and detail.

items.says: SQL or analytics depth is not listed.
items.because: Some PM postings may require it, though tools should not be added without actual experience.
